summary: Hike-in mountaintop site in Clearwater County, Idaho: cabin and crow's nest in 1914, 40-foot L-4 tower in 1934, destroyed 1961; only two telephone insulators found.

facts.design: Log cabin with a crow's nest (1914); 40-foot L-4 tower on the north point (1934)
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1961. The Idaho Fire Lookouts search found only two telephone insulators in trees near a large clearing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the Clearwater National Forest; firelookout.com gives CTPA and the Forest Lookouts page names the Clearwater Timber Protective Association. Record uses the Association; the story reports both.
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Mike Andrews for 1921; the August 1921 Clearwater Republican item names R. M. Crow at Dead Horse. The sources do not say whether both men were there that year.

notes_for_editor: Dates 1914, 1934 and 1961 agree across sources. Open conflicts: agency (National Forest vs CTPA) and 1921 staffing. Brief status 'ruins' kept, since only insulators remain. Brief coordinates (46.7363, -115.62876) were not checked against any source. The Forest Service list of Clearwater National Forest lookouts (fs.usda.gov/media/259185, June 2016) does not name Deadhorse, which fits the Association reading but is not cited. A 2022 Facebook group post and search snippets were seen only in results, not read. No access level is supported, so access is omitted.
